_comment: Powers the Sources section of the reference page. Every entry here was verified by web search before being added -- see the README for the verification note. Add new sources here rather than as bare links inside module prose, so there's one place to keep this current.

items.title: NIST FIPS 197 — Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.note: The formal U.S. federal standard defining AES-128/192/256.

items.title: NIST FIPS 186-5 — Digital Signature Standard (DSS)
items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.note: Defines RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA as NIST-approved algorithms.

items.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 — Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.note: Current as of April 2025; supersedes the older SP 800-61 Rev. 2 "Computer Security Incident Handling Guide," which NIST has withdrawn.

items.title: MITRE ATT&CK for Enterprise
items.note: Technique IDs referenced in this guide: T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact), T1489 (Service Stop), T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery), T1070.001 (Clear Windows Event Logs), T1112 (Modify Registry), T1614.001 (System Language Discovery), T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation), T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information).

items.title: Using Entropy Analysis to Find Encrypted and Packed Malware
items.publisher: Lyda, R. & Hamrock, J. — IEEE Security & Privacy, vol. 5, no. 2, pp. 40–45
items.note: 2007. The foundational paper establishing entropy analysis as a fast, family-agnostic detection technique — the basis for Module 2's entropy inspector.

items.title: #StopRansomware Guide
items.note: General prevention best practices and an incident response checklist. Updated May 2023.

items.title: AA23-165A — Understanding Ransomware Threat Actors: LockBit
Qilin: Top Ransomware Threat to SLTTs in Q2 2025
items.note: Qilin has no dedicated joint CISA #StopRansomware advisory as of this guide's last check — this CIS/MS-ISAC analysis is the closest equivalent government-affiliated source and should be treated as less formal than the AA-numbered advisories above.

items.title: DeadLock ransomware: Breaking down a Rust-based encryptor with decentralized recovery infrastructure
The Gentlemen ransomware: Dissecting a self-propagating Go encryptor
items.note: May 28, 2026. Second Module 4 example — Storm-2697, Curve25519 + XChaCha20 hybrid encryption, self-propagating.

items.title: New BYOVD loader behind DeadLock ransomware attack
items.note: Corroborating detail on the BYOVD loader component observed in some DeadLock intrusions.

items.title: Microsoft Security Blog — ransomware coverage
items.note: Ongoing feed, not a single article — this guide's case studies are a snapshot of it, not the whole picture.
